lines.en: Many errors in these have arisen from the carelessness of copyists: nevertheless, the author of Caesar's

lines.en: everywhere conflated the conflicting opinions of various Greeks among themselves,

lines.en: no one will deny that the author of the dodecaeteris could have done the same. And not even this

lines.en: do we sufficiently understand, whether the author persuaded himself that the equinoxes and solstices occurred at another time in other years.

lines.en: This indeed is most certain, that in the year of Libra the copyist falsely wrote the 23rd of Libaios,

lines.en: since the 24th day of Libaios is the same as the 25th day of the month of December.

lines.en: Therefore we both preserved the 6th day before the Kalends of January and restored the 26th of Libaios.

summary.headline: Dodecaeteris Seasonal Dates
summary.text: Corrections and commentary on the dodecaeteris calendar dates for the winter solstice, mid-winter, vernal equinox, rising of the Pleiades, and summer solstice, comparing Caesar, Eudoxus, Clodius, and Columella and citing zodiacal years and month dates.
